title: Real tool waits exposed recency benefits and output-dependent comparisons
summary: An initial two-pair repository workflow was diagnostic. A later three-repeat pressure study measured higher workflow throughput from early CPU wait hints; adding semantic retention provided no incremental gain.
scope: Pressure study: Qwen2.5-7B-AWQ, RTX 2080 Ti, decode graphs, nine cases, 576 responses and 432 actual tools. Initial study: four cases and 128 responses.
limitations: Later live prompts/outputs differ. These are closed-loop workflow results, not identical-work policy attribution. Narrow test-status correctness does not establish general answer quality.
decision: Retain actual tool waits and demonstrated cache competition as useful experimental ingredients, without fixing the product to these workloads.

chart.caption: Three whole-case paired repetitions on fixed inputs; original 95% intervals. Higher is faster.
